### Summary

An interpolation holding a ternary split across lines is reported as resolving to `any` / `unknown` when its alternate (after `:`) holds an object literal. Both branches return `string`. The same expression on one line is not reported, nor is the object literal in the consequent.

### Version

- `vize` 0.443.0 (npm, bundled `@typescript/typescript-darwin-arm64` 7.0.2)
- Node v26.10.0, macOS arm64

`vize check` reports no type errors for the same file.

### Reproduction

`vize.config.json`

```json
{
  "linter": {
    "preset": "opinionated",
    "typeAware": true
  }
}
```

`tsconfig.json`

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ESNext",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "lib": ["ESNext", "DOM"]
  },
  "include": ["*.vue", "*.ts"]
}
```

`MultilineTernary.vue`

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const t = (id: string, params?: Record<string, unknown>): string => id;
const flag = true;
const name = "x";
</script>

<template>
  <!-- reported: the alternate holds an object literal, and the ternary spans lines -->
  <p>{{
    flag
      ? t("a")
      : t("b", { name })
  }}</p>
  <!-- not reported: the same expression on one line -->
  <p>{{ flag ? t("a") : t("b", { name }) }}</p>
  <!-- not reported: the object literal in the consequent -->
  <p>{{
    flag
      ? t("b", { name })
      : t("a")
  }}</p>
</template>
```

`vize lint --format plain MultilineTernary.vue`

```
  MultilineTernary.vue:10:5 warning type/no-unsafe-template-binding Template interpolation resolves to an unsafe `any` or `unknown` type
```
